verses.1: Now Israel, listen to the statutes and the judgments I teach you to do so that you may live and go in to take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving to your fathers.
verses.2: You must not add to the word I command you, nor subtract from it, but keep the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today.
verses.3: Your eyes saw everything the LORD did to Baal Peor. Every man who followed Baal Peor the LORD your God has destroyed from your midst.
verses.4: But you who cling to the LORD your God are all alive today.
verses.5: Look, I have taught you statutes and judgments as the LORD my God commanded me, to do them in the land to which you are going to possess it.
verses.6: Keep them and do them, for they are your wisdom and understanding in the eyes of the peoples who will hear all these statutes and say, "Surely this great nation is a wise and discerning people."
verses.7: For what great nation is there that has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is whenever we call upon Him?
verses.8: What great nation is there that has statutes and judgments as righteous as all this Torah I give you today?
verses.9: Only be careful for yourselves and guard your life very much, lest you forget the things your eyes have seen and turn your heart away from them in all the days of your life. Rather, teach them to your children and to your children's children.
verses.10: The day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when He said to me, "Gather the people to me, and I will let them hear My words, that they may learn to fear Me all the days they live on the earth and teach them to their children."
verses.11: You approached and stood under the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire to the heart of the heavens—dark cloud and thick darkness.
verses.12: The LORD spoke to you from the midst of the fire—His voice you heard, but His form you did not see—only a voice.
verses.13: He declared to you His covenant that He commanded you to do, the Ten Words, and He wrote them on two stone tablets.
verses.14: And He commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and judgments to do them in the land you are crossing into to possess.
verses.15: You must guard your lives very carefully, for you did not see any form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb from the midst of the fire.
verses.16: Lest you corrupt yourselves and make for yourselves an idol, an image of anything—male or female.
verses.17: An image of any animal on the earth, an image of any bird that flies in the sky.
verses.18: An image of any creeping thing that creeps on the earth, an image of any fish that is in the water under the earth.
verses.19: Lest you lift up your eyes to the sky and see the sun and the moon and the stars, the whole host of the heavens, and be drawn away and worship them and serve them, which the LORD your God has distributed to all the nations under the whole heavens.
verses.20: But you, the LORD took you and brought you out from the house of iron, from Egypt, to be His people, His inheritance, as it is today.
verses.21: And the LORD was angry with me because of your words and swore that I would not cross the Jordan and enter the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
verses.22: For I will die in this land and will not cross the Jordan. But you will cross and possess the good land.
verses.23: Be careful for yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of the LORD your God that He made with you, and make for yourselves an idol, an image of anything the LORD your God has commanded you.
verses.24: For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.
verses.25: If you father children and children of your children, and you grow and multiply in the land, and you become corrupt and make an idol, an image of anything, and do evil in the sight of the LORD your God to provoke Him.
verses.26: I solemnly declare to you today the heavens and the earth, that you will be destroyed quickly from the land you are crossing to possess the Jordan, and you will not live long in it, but will be utterly destroyed.
verses.27: And the LORD will scatter you among all the nations, and you will be left few in number among the nations to which the LORD will lead you.
verses.28: And you will serve there gods made by human hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
verses.29: But there you will seek the LORD your God and find Him, if you search for Him with all your heart and with all your soul.
verses.30: In your distress, in the last days, when all these things have come upon you, you will return to the LORD your God and listen to His voice.
verses.31: For the LORD your God is a compassionate God. He will not abandon you, nor destroy you, nor forget the covenant He made with your fathers.
verses.32: Ask now from the days of old, from the time when God created man on the earth and from one end of the heavens to the other end—has such a great thing happened or been heard of like this?
verses.33: Has a people ever heard the voice of a god speaking from the midst of fire as you have heard and still lived?
verses.34: Or has a god ever taken one nation from another nation by trials, signs, wonders, war, a mighty hand, and an outstretched arm, and great terrors, as all the things the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
verses.35: You have seen and know that the LORD is the God, and there is no other besides Him.
verses.36: From the heavens He let His voice be heard to instruct you, and on the earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words from the midst of the fire.
verses.37: Because He loved your fathers, He chose their descendants after them. He brought you out with His great power from Egypt.
verses.38: To drive out nations greater and mightier than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as it is today.
verses.39: You must know today and turn your hearts back, that the LORD is the God in the heavens above and on the earth below, and there is no other.
verses.40: Keep His statutes and commandments that I command you today, so it may go well for you and your children after you and you may live long on the land that the LORD your God gives you for all the days.
verses.41: Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan to the east of the sun.
verses.42: For a fugitive who kills his neighbor unintentionally, not being an enemy yesterday or the day before, and who flees to one of these cities and lives.
verses.43: Bezer in the desert, in the lowland, for the Reubenites, and Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
verses.44: This is the Torah that Moses set before the sons of Israel.
verses.45: These are the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments that Moses spoke to the sons of Israel when they went out from Egypt.
verses.46: Beyond the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the sons of Israel struck when they went out from Egypt.
verses.47: And they took his land and the land of Og king of Bashan—two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan to the east of the sun.
verses.48: From Aroer, which is on the edge of the stream of Arnon, to Mount Sion, which is Hermon.
verses.49: And all the Arabah beyond the Jordan to the east, from the salt sea to the slopes of the Pisgah.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "the statutes and the judgments" — "chukim" and "mishpatim" are translated as "statutes" and "judgments" respectively, following the glossary.
- v. 19: "the whole host of the heavens" — the Hebrew "tzav'at hashamayim" is translated to reflect the celestial array as a "host."
- v. 25: "children of your children" — "b'nei banecha" is rendered to emphasize the generational depth of the warning.
- v. 32: "from the days of old" — "mikkol yamim" is translated to convey the historical breadth of the rhetorical question.
- v. 43: "Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites" — "Ramoth" is a proper name and is retained as such.
- v. 48: "Mount Sion" — "Har Sheion" is translated as "Mount Sion," which is rendered in context as "Hermon" in v. 48.
